verdict.rationale: iTerm2's own shell integration knows where prompts are, which commands you enter, the host and the current directory, and it sets marks at each prompt (docs-31, docs-8, gh-10). Separately, it can notify you of job completion so long jobs can run in the background (docs-37, docs-45), and per-line timestamps help you see how long a job took (docs-49). However, the evidence never mentions exit-status tracking or a per-command duration feature, and it does not tie the completion notifications to shell integration. Missing for 10: documented per-command exit status display, explicit command duration tracking via shell integration, notifications explicitly tied to command completion, independent hands-on corroboration.
